minutes.headline: ZBA granted dimensional variations for a 13-acre lot ground-mount solar system, on condition it goes to planning board review.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard Michael Conway's application for relief from the lot size and side setback requirements of the large-scale ground-mounted solar bylaw at 322 Flat Hill Road. Members spent much of the time framing what the board could decide versus the planning board, and discussed how virtual net metering credits work. The board voted to grant the special permit with a condition requiring development plan review by the planning board.

public_comment.topic: Resident across the road at 305 Flat Hill Road spoke in favor, describing the applicants as good neighbors.
Resident of 49 Courtland Circle said he completely supports the idea.
Raised from the floor that the request should be framed as relief from the large-scale bylaw's lot-size and setback requirements, not the system size.

votes.motion: Grant the special permit for dimensional variation for lot size, setbacks and system size, conditioned on proceeding through development plan review with the planning board (later reframed to lot size and the two side setbacks).
votes.outcome: passed, with one 'no' heard and a sixth member abstaining; exact count not stated

budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant said the project depends on state incentive structures and would be privately funded, with no grant money awaited. Credits would be allocated to buyers who see them as bill deductions.
A member suggested the applicant could make money from credits beyond his own household use; the applicant said credits could be allocated to others.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to frame the request as dimensional variations for lot size and setbacks, deferring site details to the planning board.
The permit is conditional: no work until the project has gone through development plan review by the planning board.
Applicant told the decision can be appealed within 20 days of filing and the permit should be recorded at the registry of deeds.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit for a ground-mounted solar system at 322 Flat Hill Road, with one 'no' heard and one abstention.
The permit is conditional: no work may begin until the project has gone through development plan review by the planning board.
The vote was framed as relief from the lot size and the two side setbacks of the large-scale solar bylaw, not the size of the system.
Members agreed to limit the decision to lot size and setbacks and leave site details to the planning board.
The applicant was told the decision can be appealed within 20 days of filing and the permit should be recorded at the registry of deeds.

why_it_matters: The project can move forward only after planning board review, so neighbors on Flat Hill Road will have another public step where site details such as sight lines and screening are decided.
The board noted a gap between its authority and the planning board's under the large-scale solar bylaw, which could affect how future solar applications are handled.
watch_next: Development plan review by the planning board, required before any work begins.
The 20-day appeal period after the decision is filed.
